- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > history peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +20% above recent peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if yes, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), check if sentiment was bearish — if yes, apply upward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., dropping from 80+ to 70+), forecast should be adjusted downward 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
